validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. (1) https://www.zhylyoigas.kz/upload/iblock/7dc/7dcb03c674d4e9b9700d85eb49ce1c59.pdf — TOO Zhylyoigas's own Q3-2019 'reserve/free capacity' filing states in its opening paragraph: 'Товарный газ поступает по подземному магистральному газопроводу Кульсары - Тенгиз диаметром 1200 мм на ГРС в количестве 5-ед...' ('Commercial gas arrives via the underground trunk gas pipeline Kulsary-Tengiz, diameter 1200 mm, to 5 GDS units...'). Zhylyoigas is the real gas-distribution utility for Zhylyoi district, Atyrau region (self-description on https://www.zhylyoigas.kz/ru/company/? verified live: 'газоснабжающая компания, эксплуатирующая магистральные и распределительные газопроводы... на территории Жылыойского района Атырауской области'), i.e. exactly the GEM end-point (Kulsary). This is a primary operator/downstream-customer document, not a GEM-derived tertiary source. (2) GulfPub PE World Map (Tier 2, scraped 2025-12-11) independently carries the SAME pipe under the SAME name 'Tengiz - Kulsary' (two OIDs, 1273 and 5640 — near-duplicate GulfPub entries for the one physical line, a GulfPub-internal issue, not a GEM duplicate), operator/owner QazaqGaz, status Operating, geodesic Tengiz-field-to-Kulsary distance ~102 km (consistent with a 126-130 km pipe route). Two independent origins agree the line exists, runs Tengiz oil field -> Kulsary, and is operated/owned by the QazaqGaz group (Intergas Central Asia / Zhylyoigas being its ATyrau-region operating arms) -> EXISTENCE = high confidence. CLASSIFICATION: the Zhylyoigas filing itself calls it 'подземный магистральный газопровод' (underground TRUNK gas pipeline) — matches GEM's PipelineType=transmission; it feeds a downstream distribution network (5 GDS/ГРС units, 476.71 km of local mains) rather than being a gathering/process line itself, so 'transmission' (trunk, feeding local distribution) is correct, not a feeder/gathering line. DUPLICATE: checked against the 39-row Kazakhstan-gas roster — no other row is named 'Tengiz-Kulsary' or shares its Tengiz-field-to-Kulsary endpoints; not one of the flagged redundancy clusters (P3948/P5784, P1124/P2299/P2300, P2291/P5770/P5771, P2289/P5695, P5927/P5928, P0739/P5810, P1476/P3999, P6830/P6831, P3964/P5901) — none of those involve P6835. Distinct, non-duplicate row.

GEM's Diameter (1200 mm) and Capacity (0.83 bcm/y) are both corroborated by the primary Zhylyoigas filing; GulfPub disagrees on both and its own capacity field is flagged unreliable by GulfPub itself.
validity.researcher_notes: DIAMETER: GEM=1200 mm. The Zhylyoigas primary filing states the diameter explicitly and unambiguously as '1200 мм' — exact match (this is a scanned/image-only PDF per `pdfimages -list` [2496x3510, 300 ppi native, single JPEG, not upsampled], so url_verifier's text-substring check FAILs on '0.83'/'Тенгиз' as expected for an image PDF — content confirmed by direct visual read of the page, not text extraction; same false-negative pattern documented in url_verifier's docstring). GulfPub's two matched OIDs (1273, 5640) both give diameter='28.0' (28 in = 711 mm) — a large, material disagreement with GEM. I side with GEM/the primary source here: it is the actual downstream operator describing the exact line that feeds its own stations, whereas GulfPub's per-row source_url (https://qazaqgaz.kz/en/obshchaya-informaciya, verified live) turns out to be a generic QazaqGaz 'about us' page with no mention of 'Tengiz' at all — i.e. a boilerplate URL attached to many GulfPub rows, not a pipeline-specific citation, so GulfPub's number here carries little weight. CAPACITY: GEM=0.83 bcm/y. Not literally stated in the Zhylyoigas filing, but derivable from it: the filing's own table gives combined design ('проектная мощность') throughput for the 5 GDS units fed by this trunk line = 50,000+20,000+10,000+5,000+10,000 = 95,000 m3/h, and the filing separately states 'общей пропускной способностью 95 000 м3/ч' for the same trunk-to-GDS handoff. Annualized: 95,000 m3/h x 8,760 h/yr = 832,200,000 m3/yr = 0.8322 bcm/yr -- matches GEM's 0.83 almost exactly (rounds identically). This is a strong but SINGLE-SOURCE, DERIVED (not literally-stated) corroboration, and it measures the downstream distribution hand-off capacity, not necessarily the trunk pipe's own transport capacity, so treat as a caveat rather than an exact independent match. GulfPub's capacity field for this row (800 MMcf/d = ~8.27 bcm/y, ~10x GEM's value) materially conflicts, but GulfPub's own 'capacity_raw' field for both OIDs literally reads 'Not specified' — i.e. the 800.0 numeric is GulfPub's own estimate/default, not a reported figure (confirmed: capacity values are NOT a shared constant across the country's GulfPub rows, so this isn't the known Capacity_mmcfd=300 placeholder, but the explicit 'Not specified' raw-text flag means it is not independent evidence and should not be read as a real conflict). LENGTH: GEM=126.00 km; GulfPub gives 130.357 km on both matched OIDs (~3.4% longer) and geodesic Tengiz-field-to-Kulsary is ~102 km, consistent with a non-straight ~126-130 km routed pipe. No primary source found that states an exact trunk length (the Zhylyoigas filing only gives the LOCAL distribution-network total, 476.71 km, of which just 1.936 km is coded 'магистральные газопроводы' -- that 1.936 km is Zhylyoigas's own short trunk TIE-IN segment near its GDS units, not the ~126 km cross-country Tengiz-to-Kulsary run, which is evidently owned/operated further upstream (QazaqGaz/Intergas) and outside Zhylyoigas's own asset register). Net: length sits within Tier-2-only tolerance (single source, ~3%), acceptable but not independently pinned down by a primary source.
